 PS5 Pro live restock tracker: Where to buy the best console for 'GTA 6'
 Finding a PS5 Pro at retail price feels like a heist of its own.

 If you waited until launch week to upgrade your console before GTA 6 arrives on Nov. 19, you are not alone. With Rockstar’s biggest release in over a decade just days away, gamers across the country are scrambling to lock down Sony’s most powerful hardware — and that sudden rush has wiped out PlayStation 5 Pro inventory almost everywhere.
 Following Sony’s April price hike that pushed the PS5 Pro’s standard MSRP to $899.99, legitimate retail stock has dried up across PlayStation Direct, Best Buy, Target, and GameStop. 
 Instead of falling for inflated reseller markups, bookmark this tracker to monitor official retail pages directly. While major storefronts are currently sitting at zero, brief restock waves at the standard list price continue to cycle through — and having the right links ready is the easiest way to snag one before Vice City opens its doors.

 Where to track down a PS5 Pro at retail price
 If you are trying to score a PS5 Pro for retail price before GTA 6 arrives, save these direct store links and check them regularly — inventory drops in brief, unpredictable waves:
 Amazon — Currently out of stock, unless you opt for marked-up listings from third-party sellers.
 Best Buy — Currently out of stock. Online drops typically filter buyers through a virtual queue, so stay logged into your account ahead of time. Keep an eye on local store pickup toggles too, as single units occasionally surface regionally.
 GameStop — New consoles are sold out online, so calling or walking into your neighborhood store is your best bet for retail-priced stock. Just ignore the pre-owned listings — the retailer deliberately jacked used and refurbished units up to $1,399.99 ($500 more than a brand-new box) to cash in on the GTA 6 shortage. Hard pass.
 PlayStation Direct — Currently out of stock. Buying straight from Sony is your cleanest shot at paying the list price without third-party clutter, and they cap orders at one console per customer whenever new batches go live.
 Target — Currently out of stock. Target tends to release small online waves alongside early-morning store pickup inventory tied to local freight arrivals. Having payment details saved in the Target app saves crucial seconds at checkout.
 Walmart — Currently out of stock, unless you opt for marked-up listings from third-party sellers.
 Why everyone is scrambling for a PS5 Pro right now
 It all comes down to GTA 6 arriving next week. Since Rockstar is launching the game exclusively on consoles with no PC version available at launch, anyone who wants the best-looking trip to Leonida is rushing to grab Sony's flagship hardware.
 Rockstar confirmed this week that while GTA 6 runs at 30 frames per second across all consoles, the PS5 Pro is the single best place to play on day one. It is the only console getting sharper 4K visuals through PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) and upgraded ray-traced shadows. Throw in faster load times, DualSense controller haptics, and a built-in 2TB drive for massive game files, and it makes total sense why players are upgrading right now.

 Besides that, supply has been tight for months. Component shortages and rising memory costs have slowed down console production throughout 2026 , leaving stores without enough stock to handle the pre-launch rush. Because production won't catch up to GTA 6 hype anytime soon, any standard list-price units that hit store sites will vanish in minutes.

 Is the PS5 Pro worth the upgrade?
 If you are debating whether to hunt down a PS5 Pro instead of playing GTA 6 on a standard PlayStation 5, Rockstar just confirmed exactly what the extra hardware gets you on day one.
 Even though frame rates remain the same across all consoles, the PS5 Pro is the only system to unlock two major visual upgrades. First is PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR), Sony’s AI upscaling tech that sharpens lower-resolution images on the fly so Vice City’s neon skylines, crowded beaches, and distant horizons look noticeably crisper on a 4K TV.
 You also get exclusive ray-traced shadows powered by the Pro’s faster graphics chip, giving sunlight, headlights, and towering cityscapes far more realistic depth and lighting than you will see on a base PS5 or Xbox Series X. Plus, with GTA 6 taking up over 210GB, the PS5 Pro’s built-in 2TB SSD gives you plenty of breathing room without having to delete half your library just to install it.

 How to beat the bots and improve your chances of finding stock
 Catching a surprise drop before GTA 6 launches comes down to speed and a little bit of prep:
 Dodge third-party marketplace sellers: Sites like Walmart and Amazon let outside merchants charge whatever they want. Always check the "Sold and shipped by" label to ensure you are buying from the actual retailer at standard list price.
 Save your checkout information beforehand: Taking the time to type in a security code or shipping address during a drop will cost you your cart. Keep your profiles logged in with default payment methods saved.
 Do not refresh Best Buy's waiting line: When Best Buy runs a drop, it puts shoppers into an automated queue. Hitting refresh resets your spot and sends you to the very back of the line. Meanwhile, refreshing PlayStation Direct directly on weekday mornings often catches small waves before stock-alert apps fire.
 Check physical stores in the morning: Online checkout bots can wipe out digital inventory in seconds. Visiting Target, Best Buy, or GameStop when doors open often turns up fresh shipment boxes that never made it onto website listings.
 Should you wait for a PS5 Pro Black Friday deal?
 In short: no. While major retailers almost always hold back small batches of high-demand hardware to anchor their Thanksgiving week and Black Friday doorbusters, don't expect a holiday discount on the PS5 Pro this year.
 Sony's early Black Friday rollout has focused almost entirely on digital games and accessories rather than new console markdowns — so simply catching a legitimate restock at the standard list price is the real Black Friday win.
 Waiting until Nov. 27 also puts you up against peak holiday traffic, GTA 6 latecomers, and automated checkout bots all hammering store servers at once. If an "Add to Cart" button flickers live at $899.99 before Thanksgiving week officially kicks off, buy it on the spot instead of waiting around for a sale that isn't coming.
